questions.text: Which of the following has the dimensions of pressure?
questions.explanation: Pressure = force/area = MLT⁻² ÷ L² = ML⁻¹T⁻². MLT⁻² is force and ML²T⁻² is energy.

questions.text: Two perpendicular forces of 6 N and 8 N act on a body at a point. The magnitude of their resultant is
questions.explanation: For perpendicular forces, R = √(6² + 8²) = √100 = 10 N.

questions.text: A uniform metre rule is pivoted at its centre. An 8 N weight hung 20 cm from the pivot is balanced by a weight hung 40 cm from the pivot on the other side. The balancing weight is
questions.explanation: By the principle of moments, 8 × 20 = W × 40, so W = 160 ÷ 40 = 4 N.

questions.text: The area under a velocity-time graph represents
questions.explanation: Area = velocity × time = distance. The gradient of the graph gives acceleration.

questions.text: A temperature of 77 °F is equivalent to
A simple pendulum of length 1 m oscillates with a period of approximately [g = 10 m/s², π = 3.14]
A car accelerates uniformly from rest at 2 m/s² for 5 s. The distance it covers is
A block of mass 5 kg rests on a horizontal surface. If the coefficient of limiting friction is 0.4, the limiting frictional force is [g = 10 m/s²]
A spring extends by 4 cm when an 8 N load is hung on it. Assuming Hooke's law is obeyed, the extension produced by a 20 N load is
questions.explanation: Extension is proportional to load: e = 4 × 20 ÷ 8 = 10 cm.

questions.text: A machine lifts a load of 50 kg through a vertical height of 4 m in 5 s. The power developed is [g = 10 m/s²]
questions.explanation: Work = mgh = 50 × 10 × 4 = 2000 J; power = work/time = 2000 ÷ 5 = 400 W.

questions.text: A wire 2 m long of cross-sectional area 1 mm² extends by 1 mm when a force of 200 N is applied. Young's modulus of the material is
questions.explanation: Stress = 200 ÷ 10⁻⁶ = 2 × 10⁸ Pa; strain = 10⁻³ ÷ 2 = 5 × 10⁻⁴; Y = stress/strain = 2 × 10⁸ ÷ 5 × 10⁻⁴ = 4.0 × 10¹¹ Pa.

questions.text: In a hydraulic press, the small piston has an area of 0.02 m² and the large piston an area of 0.4 m². A force of 50 N applied to the small piston lifts a load of
questions.explanation: Pressure is transmitted equally, so F₂ = F₁ × A₂/A₁ = 50 × 0.4 ÷ 0.02 = 1000 N.

questions.text: A 2 kg mass falls freely from a height of 10 m. Its kinetic energy just before it hits the ground is [g = 10 m/s²]
questions.explanation: Loss of potential energy = gain in kinetic energy = mgh = 2 × 10 × 10 = 200 J.

questions.text: A force of 200 N acts uniformly on an area of 0.5 m². The pressure exerted is
The quantity of heat required to raise the temperature of 2 kg of water by 20 K is [specific heat capacity of water = 4200 J/kg K]
The pressure at a depth of 5 m below the surface of water of density 1000 kg/m³ is [g = 10 m/s²]
The saturated vapour pressure of a liquid depends only on its
questions.explanation: At a given temperature the saturated vapour pressure is fixed, whatever the volume or amount of liquid present, as long as liquid and vapour coexist.

questions.text: 0.5 kg of water at 80 °C is mixed with 0.5 kg of water at 20 °C in an insulated container. Neglecting heat losses, the final temperature of the mixture is
questions.explanation: Equal masses of the same liquid reach the mean temperature: (80 + 20) ÷ 2 = 50 °C.

questions.text: Heat can travel through a vacuum by
questions.explanation: Conduction and convection need a material medium. Radiation is electromagnetic and travels through empty space, as heat from the Sun does.

questions.text: A steel rod 2 m long is heated through a temperature rise of 50 K. If the linear expansivity of steel is 1.2 × 10⁻⁵ K⁻¹, the increase in length is
A fixed mass of gas at 2 atm occupies 3 litres. If it is compressed isothermally to 1.5 litres, its new pressure is
questions.explanation: By Boyle's law, P₁V₁ = P₂V₂, so P₂ = 2 × 3 ÷ 1.5 = 4 atm.

questions.text: The quantity of heat needed to melt 0.5 kg of ice at 0 °C is [specific latent heat of fusion of ice = 3.34 × 10⁵ J/kg]
questions.explanation: Q = mL = 0.5 × 3.34 × 10⁵ = 1.67 × 10⁵ J. The temperature stays constant during melting.

questions.text: The pitch of a musical note depends mainly on the
questions.explanation: Pitch rises with frequency. Amplitude determines loudness, and speed in a given medium is constant.

questions.text: The bending of waves around the edges of an obstacle is called
questions.explanation: Diffraction is the spreading of waves around obstacles and through openings. Refraction is bending due to a change of speed in a new medium.

questions.text: A wave of frequency 50 Hz has a wavelength of 4 m. Its speed is
An echo is heard 0.4 s after a shout in front of a cliff. If the speed of sound in air is 340 m/s, the distance of the cliff from the observer is
questions.explanation: The sound travels to the cliff and back, so 2d = vt = 340 × 0.4 = 136 m, giving d = 68 m.

questions.text: An object is placed 20 cm in front of a plane mirror. The distance between the object and its image is
questions.explanation: The image forms as far behind the mirror as the object is in front, so object-to-image distance is 20 + 20 = 40 cm.

questions.text: A ray of light passes from air into glass of refractive index 1.5 at an angle of incidence of 60°. The angle of refraction is approximately [sin 60° = 0.866]
Optical fibres transmit light signals by the principle of
questions.explanation: Light inside the fibre strikes the core-cladding boundary at angles greater than the critical angle and is totally internally reflected along the fibre.

questions.text: Which of the following electromagnetic waves has the highest frequency?
questions.explanation: In the electromagnetic spectrum, frequency increases from radio waves to gamma rays, which have the highest frequency and shortest wavelength.

questions.text: Two point charges of 2 μC and 3 μC are placed 0.3 m apart in air. The electrostatic force between them is [k = 9 × 10⁹ N m²/C²]
questions.explanation: F = kq₁q₂/r² = (9 × 10⁹ × 2 × 10⁻⁶ × 3 × 10⁻⁶) ÷ 0.09 = 0.054 ÷ 0.09 = 0.6 N, repulsive since the charges are alike.

questions.text: Two 6 μF capacitors are connected in series. Their equivalent capacitance is
A 100 W electric bulb is used for 5 hours. The electrical energy consumed is
questions.explanation: Energy = power × time = 0.1 kW × 5 h = 0.5 kWh.

questions.text: A convex lens of focal length 10 cm forms an image of an object placed 30 cm from it. The image distance is
Lenz's law, which states that an induced current opposes the change producing it, is a consequence of the law of conservation of
questions.explanation: If the induced current aided the change, energy would be created. Lenz's law ensures the induced effects oppose the change, conserving energy.

questions.text: Cathode rays are streams of
questions.explanation: Cathode rays are fast-moving electrons emitted from the cathode of a discharge tube; they are deflected by electric and magnetic fields.

questions.text: A 3 Ω resistor and a 6 Ω resistor are connected in parallel. Their equivalent resistance is
A cell of e.m.f. 2 V and internal resistance 0.5 Ω is connected to an external resistor of 3.5 Ω. The current in the circuit is
An alternating voltage has a peak value of 282.8 V. Its root-mean-square value is
A 12 V battery drives a current of 0.4 A through a resistor. The resistance of the resistor is
questions.explanation: By Ohm's law, R = V/I = 12 ÷ 0.4 = 30 Ω.

questions.text: A closed organ pipe of length 0.85 m resonates in its fundamental mode. If the speed of sound in air is 340 m/s, the fundamental frequency is
questions.explanation: For a closed pipe, L = λ/4, so λ = 3.4 m and f = v/λ = 340 ÷ 3.4 = 100 Hz.

questions.text: When a wire is stretched beyond its elastic limit, it will
questions.explanation: Beyond the elastic limit the material deforms plastically and does not recover its original length when the load is removed.

questions.text: The region around a magnet within which its magnetic influence can be felt is called the
questions.explanation: The magnetic field is the space around a magnet where magnetic forces act. Flux is the total field passing through an area, and poles are the ends of the magnet.

questions.text: An ideal transformer has 2000 turns in its primary coil and 100 turns in its secondary coil. If the primary voltage is 220 V, the secondary voltage is
The random, haphazard movement of smoke particles in air provides evidence for
options: the law of conservation of energy
questions.explanation: Brownian movement shows that invisible air molecules are in constant random motion, colliding with the smoke particles, as the kinetic theory predicts.

questions.text: When white light passes through a triangular glass prism, the colour that is deviated the most is
questions.explanation: Violet light has the shortest wavelength and the highest refractive index in glass, so it bends most; red bends least.

questions.text: A fixed mass of gas at a pressure of 100 kPa and temperature 300 K is heated at constant volume to 600 K. Its new pressure is
questions.explanation: At constant volume, P/T is constant, so P₂ = 100 × 600 ÷ 300 = 200 kPa.

questions.text: In simple harmonic motion, the acceleration of the oscillating body is greatest at
questions.explanation: Acceleration is proportional to displacement from equilibrium, so it is maximum where displacement is greatest, at the extremes.

questions.text: A radioactive sample has a half-life of 4 days. What fraction of the original sample remains after 12 days?
questions.explanation: 12 days is 3 half-lives, so the fraction remaining is (1/2)³ = 1/8.

questions.text: A p-n junction diode conducts electric current appreciably only when it is
questions.explanation: Forward bias lowers the potential barrier and allows a large current. Reverse bias widens the barrier and only a tiny leakage current flows.

questions.text: A 2 kg mass moving at 3 m/s collides with a stationary 4 kg mass and they move together afterwards. Their common velocity is
questions.explanation: By conservation of momentum, 2 × 3 = (2 + 4)v, so v = 6 ÷ 6 = 1 m/s.

questions.text: Light of photon energy 5 eV falls on a metal whose work function is 2 eV. The maximum kinetic energy of the emitted photoelectrons is
questions.explanation: By Einstein's photoelectric equation, KEmax = hf − W = 5 − 2 = 3 eV.

questions.text: Which of the following is a scalar quantity?
questions.explanation: Speed has magnitude only. Velocity, acceleration and momentum have both magnitude and direction.

questions.text: The chemical energy in an electric cell is converted into electrical energy by
options: chemical action between the electrodes and the electrolyte
questions.explanation: A cell produces e.m.f. through chemical reactions at its electrodes. Induction generates e.m.f. in generators, and the photoelectric effect involves light ejecting electrons.

questions.text: A machine has a velocity ratio of 5 and an efficiency of 80%. Its mechanical advantage is
questions.explanation: Efficiency = MA/VR, so MA = 0.80 × 5 = 4.

questions.text: The weight of a 60 kg mass on the Moon, where the acceleration due to gravity is 1.6 m/s², is
questions.explanation: W = mg = 60 × 1.6 = 96 N. Mass stays 60 kg, but weight changes with g.

questions.text: The formation of sharp shadows is evidence that light
questions.explanation: Shadows with sharp edges form because light travels in straight lines and cannot bend around the obstacle; this is rectilinear propagation.

questions.text: The force that keeps a body moving in a circular path, directed towards the centre of the circle, is the
questions.explanation: Centripetal force acts towards the centre and provides the inward acceleration. Centrifugal force is the apparent outward effect felt in the rotating frame.

questions.text: A passenger in a car lurches forward when the driver brakes suddenly because of
questions.explanation: By Newton's first law, the passenger's body tends to continue moving forward at the car's former speed until a force stops it; this tendency is inertia.

questions.text: In a hydroelectric power station, the sequence of energy conversions is
questions.explanation: Water stored behind the dam has gravitational potential energy, which becomes kinetic energy as it falls and drives turbines that generate electricity.
